What is framed New York wall art?

Framed New York wall art refers to printed artwork depicting NYC scenes — such as the Manhattan skyline, neighbourhood streets, or city landmarks — presented as ready-to-display art prints, often sold as curated sets. At AboutWallArt, our framed New York wall art prints are produced in the UK on quality art paper using fade-resistant pigment inks, and the framed options arrive ready to hang straight out of the box. Sets of three are particularly popular for creating a gallery-style display above a fireplace or sofa, giving a cohesive, travel-inspired look without the effort of sourcing a matching frame. Whether you love the Big Apple, Manhattan, or simply the warm aesthetic of NYC-inspired illustration, these prints make it easy to bring that city energy into your home.

How to Hang a Set of 3 New York Wall Art Prints Above a Fireplace

1. Measure your wall space: Start by measuring the width of your fireplace or chimney breast. Divide this by three (for a set of three prints) to get a rough maximum width per print, then subtract around 5–8 cm per gap between them. This tells you the ideal print size before you order.

2. Mark your hanging points: Use a spirit level and pencil to mark three evenly spaced horizontal points at your chosen height — typically so the centre of each print sits roughly at eye level (around 145–150 cm from the floor). Even spacing between prints (5–8 cm) looks the most polished.

3. Hang the centre print first: Always start with the middle print, then work outward to the left and right. This keeps the arrangement symmetrical and makes it much easier to adjust if needed.

4. Step back and check: Once all three are up, step back to the other side of the room and check alignment. A small adjustment now saves a lot of fussing later. Use removable adhesive strips on lighter prints if you want flexibility to reposition.

5. Style the mantel below: Complement your new NYC wall art prints with warm accessories on the mantel — think dried autumn stems, amber glass candle holders, or a small stack of travel books — to echo the ochre and charcoal tones in the artwork.

Framed New York Wall Art Prints — Which Option Is Right for You?

Format — Unframed Print: The art print only, printed on your choice of Luster or Museum quality paper. You source and select your own frame. Perfect if you already have frames at home or want a very specific frame style.

Format — Framed Print: Your chosen art print mounted and framed, arriving completely ready to hang. Saves time and guarantees a neat, finished result. Available in multiple sizes with a choice of Luster or Museum quality paper.

Format — Wrapped Canvas: The artwork printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame — no print or glazing, just the image wrapped around the edges. Arrives ready to hang and suits a more relaxed, contemporary or rustic interior feel.

Paper finish (prints only) — Luster: A semi-sheen surface that reduces glare while keeping colours vibrant. A great all-rounder, especially in rooms with natural light or lamp light near the fireplace.

Paper finish (prints only) — Museum Quality: A premium fine-art paper with deeper, richer colour saturation. Ideal if you want the ochre and mustard tones of the autumn New York scenes to really stand out. Best suited to collectors or those who want a true fine-art feel.

Dining room wall art decor refers to prints, paintings, canvases or other decorative artwork chosen specifically to enhance the walls of a dining room — creating atmosphere, personality and a sense of style in the space where you eat and entertain. It can be a single statement piece or, as is very popular right now, a coordinated set of prints hung together as a group. Sets of art prints are a particularly practical choice because the prints are produced to coordinate perfectly, taking the guesswork out of creating a cohesive look.

How to Hang Dining Room Wall Art Decor: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Measure your wall space: Before ordering, measure the width of the wall or furniture you plan to hang above (such as a sideboard or dining table). Aim for your set of prints — including the gaps between them — to span roughly two thirds of that width for a balanced, well-proportioned look.

2. Choose your size and finish: Consider how much natural light the room gets. Luster paper suits brighter rooms and makes warm tones pop; Museum quality paper gives a matte gallery finish that works beautifully with softer, more diffused light. Wrapped canvas suits a contemporary, frameless look.

4. Hang at eye level: The centre of your art should ideally sit at roughly 145 to 150 cm from the floor — standard eye level for most adults. If hanging above furniture, aim for the bottom of the prints to sit around 15 to 20 cm above the top of the piece beneath.

5. Step back and adjust: Once hung, step back and check the overall arrangement from across the room. Small adjustments now save a lot of fiddling later — and a well-hung set of prints makes an enormous difference to how the whole room feels.

Unframed Print on Museum Quality Paper — Ideal if you prefer a softer, more matte finish with a fine-art, gallery feel. The watercolour illustration style of this autumn New York set looks particularly refined on Museum quality paper. Again, framing is your choice.

Framed Print (Luster or Museum quality) — The most convenient option — your prints arrive ready to hang straight out of the box, with no need to source frames separately. A brilliant time-saver, and you can be confident the frame size is a perfect fit for the print.

Wrapped Canvas — A contemporary, frameless option where the print is stretched and wrapped around a wooden frame. No glazing, no frame needed — just hang and enjoy. Works especially well in relaxed, modern or Scandi-style dining rooms where a clean, unfussy look is the goal.

aiItems.content:
What is travel wall art decor?

Travel wall art decor refers to art prints and wall pieces that celebrate destinations, cities, landscapes, and the joy of exploring the world — designed to be displayed in your home. They typically feature illustrated, photographic, or painterly depictions of iconic places, streets, skylines, and local scenes. Travel wall art decor is a popular choice for hallways, living rooms, and home offices, where it adds personality and a sense of adventure to any space. Sets of coordinating prints — like this New York City autumn trio — are particularly popular because they create a cohesive, curated look without the effort of sourcing individual pieces separately.

How to Hang Travel Wall Art Decor in a Hallway

1. Measure your wall first: Use a tape measure to note the width of the wall space you have available. For a set of 3 prints hung in a row, add the widths of all three prints plus the gaps between them (aim for 5–8 cm between each) and check it fits comfortably within your wall width, leaving a little breathing room at each side.

2. Find the right hanging height: The centre of each print should sit roughly at eye level — around 145–150 cm from the floor works well for most people. If you're hanging the prints above a console table or hallway bench, position the bottom of the prints about 15–20 cm above the furniture for a balanced look.

3. Mark before you hammer: Cut pieces of paper to the exact print size and use low-tack tape to hold them to the wall in your chosen arrangement. Step back and check the spacing and height look right before you make any holes — it saves a lot of fiddly adjustments later.

4. Hang and level: Use a small spirit level as you hang each print to keep them perfectly aligned. For lightweight unframed prints, picture-hanging strips are a great damage-free option; for heavier framed prints, a proper wall hook or nail into a stud will give the most secure hold.

Unframed Print — The print is delivered rolled or flat, ready for you to frame in your own choice of frame. Best if you already have a frame style in mind, or want to keep costs down. Available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Framed Print — The print arrives mounted and framed, ready to hang straight away — no need to source a frame separately. A great time-saver and makes a lovely gift. Available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper, with multiple size options.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched around a solid frame — no glass, no border, just the image edge to edge. Gives a more contemporary, frameless finish and is particularly suited to modern or minimalist interiors. Available in multiple size options.

Luster Art Paper — A semi-gloss finish with rich, vibrant colour reproduction and a gentle sheen. Handles mixed lighting well and is a versatile all-rounder for most homes.

Museum Quality Paper — A premium fine-art finish with greater depth and tonal range, ideal for bringing out the fine detail and brushwork in watercolour-style illustrations like these NYC prints. The top choice if you want the very best print quality.

As a rough guide, measure the width of your sofa or the piece of furniture below the wall, and aim for the three prints together to span roughly two-thirds of that width. If your living room has high ceilings or a large feature wall, go for one of the bigger size options — the illustrated detail in these prints really rewards a larger format, especially the coffee shop scene in the centre with all its lovely little touches.

In terms of colour, the ochre and amber tones here are warm and grounding, so they suit rooms with neutral, earthy or nature-inspired palettes really well. They can also add a welcome pop of warmth to a cooler, grey-toned room — that contrast is actually really striking. The cream-white background on each print means they won't fight with your walls whatever colour they are. And if you're choosing between Luster and Museum quality paper, Museum gives you a slightly richer depth of colour which I think suits the painterly style of this artwork especially well. Scroll down to see how each size looks in a living room before you decide — there's a handy size-guide image below showing every option in a real room setting.

What are large paintings for living room wall?

Large paintings for living room wall are oversized or statement-scale art prints designed to fill and anchor the main wall of a living space, typically displayed above a sofa, fireplace or console table. They are usually sold as single statement pieces or coordinating sets of two or three prints that together create one cohesive visual. In modern home decor, the term covers everything from canvas-wrapped prints to framed art prints on high-quality paper, and they do not need to be hand-painted originals — high-quality art prints reproduce illustrated and painted artwork with impressive fidelity. Choosing the right large wall art is one of the fastest ways to define the mood and personality of a living room, giving the space a genuine focal point that ties furniture, colour and style together.

How to Hang Large Paintings for Living Room Wall — a Simple Step-by-Step

1. Measure your wall space first: Before ordering, measure the width of the wall or the furniture beneath it. For a set of 3 prints, aim for the combined width of all three (including gaps) to cover roughly two-thirds of the sofa or sideboard width below — this creates a balanced, intentional look rather than prints that appear to float or get lost.

2. Choose your size and format: Decide whether you want unframed prints (great if you have a specific frame style in mind), framed prints (ready to hang immediately), or wrapped canvas (for a more contemporary, frame-free look). Scroll down on this page to see how each size looks in a real living room using our size-guide image.

3. Mark your hanging points carefully: Hold the centre print up to the wall first and mark its ideal position at eye level — roughly 145–150 cm from floor to the centre of the print is a good rule of thumb. Then measure outward from the centre print to position the two flanking prints with equal gaps between them (3–5 cm works well for a cohesive set).

4. Use a spirit level: Even a small tilt is very noticeable with a set of three prints in a row. Use a spirit level or a free spirit-level app on your phone to make sure all three are perfectly aligned before you fix them to the wall.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, step back across the room and check the arrangement from a distance — this is where small tweaks to height or spacing make a real difference to the final result.

Which Format Is Right for You? Comparing Your Options

Unframed Print — The print is delivered rolled or flat, ready for you to frame in your own choice of frame. Best for: buyers who already have frames, want a specific frame colour, or are ordering multiple sets and want a consistent custom-framed look throughout their home.

Framed Print — The art print arrives ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra trips to the frame shop needed. Best for: buyers who want a quick, hassle-free result and a polished, finished look immediately. Available in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, with the image wrapping around the edges. No glazing, no frame required. Best for: buyers who prefer a more contemporary, gallery-style look without the reflection of glass.

Luster Paper (for unframed and framed prints) — A semi-gloss finish that gives punchy, vivid colour with a slight sheen. Great in rooms where you want the colours to really sing.

Museum Quality Paper (for unframed and framed prints) — A premium fine-art paper with a smooth, low-sheen finish that gives greater depth and richness of colour. Particularly well-suited to illustrated and painterly artwork like this NYC autumn set, where the subtle tonal detail really benefits from a fine-art surface.

aiItems.content:
What is unique office wall decor?

Unique office wall decor refers to art prints, illustrations or wall pieces chosen specifically to personalise and inspire a workspace, going beyond generic or corporate imagery. Rather than plain motivational posters, unique office wall decor reflects individual taste — whether that is travel scenes, illustrated cityscapes, botanical prints or abstract colour work. The goal is to create an environment that feels genuinely personal, motivating and pleasant to spend time in. A well-chosen set of prints, like a travel-themed NYC collection, can make even a home office feel considered, curated and distinctly yours.

How to Choose and Hang Unique Office Wall Decor

1. Measure your wall space first: Use a tape measure or hold sheets of paper up to the wall to map out how much space you have. For a row of three prints, allow for the width of all three pieces plus the gaps between them — typically 5–8 cm between each print works well.

2. Pick a colour anchor: Choose prints that share at least one colour with something already in your office — your desk, a plant pot, a cushion on a chair. With the Autumn in New York set, the warm ochre tones anchor beautifully with natural wood desks, sage green accessories or warm white walls.

3. Decide on your arrangement: A straight horizontal row at eye level is the simplest and most effective layout for a set of three. If your wall is taller than it is wide, try a staggered or vertical arrangement instead.

4. Choose your format: Decide whether you want the prints unframed (so you can source your own frame), framed (ready to hang immediately), or on wrapped canvas for a more textured, contemporary feel.

5. Hang and adjust: Use a spirit level to keep things straight. Step back and adjust the gaps until the arrangement feels balanced — small tweaks make a big difference to the finished look.

Choosing Your Format: Office Wall Art Print Options Compared

Unframed Print on Luster Art Paper — A crisp, slightly sheen finish that makes ochre tones and illustrated detail pop under office lighting. You choose and source your own frame. Great if you already have frames or want full control over the finish.

Unframed Print on Museum Quality Paper — The richest, most gallery-like result with deeper colour reproduction and exceptional detail clarity. Also unframed — ideal if you want to display in a high-end frame of your own choosing.

Framed Print — Comes ready to hang straight out of the box — no frame hunting, no measuring, no fuss. Available in multiple sizes with your choice of Luster or Museum quality paper inside. The most convenient option for busy offices.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame with the image wrapping around the edges. Arrives ready to hang and has a tactile, studio quality that suits contemporary and creative office spaces particularly well. No glass, no frame needed.
